summary: A Fairbanks man was charged with two felonies after an arrest on Gillam Way on Friday, and felony charges were also filed over a theft on the Johansen Expressway and property damage at North Pole. The court set three competency hearings for the same hour on Friday morning and ordered a warrant in each one after the defendants did not appear; a first-degree murder charge was dismissed after a finding that the defendant was not competent to stand trial.

entries.title: Fairbanks man charged with two felonies after Gillam Way arrest
body: John Edward Raymond, 36, was arrested at the 1400 block of Gillam Way in Fairbanks at 7:47 a.m. on Oct. 16, according to the Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin.

The court file records two counts, both Class C felonies and both dated Oct. 16: assault in the third degree, for committing an assault in the fourth degree with two or more prior convictions, which the file flags as domestic violence related; and failure to stop at the direction of an officer with reckless driving. The charging document is a city police complaint.

An arraignment held on the afternoon of Oct. 16 was continued, and a further arraignment is set for Oct. 17 at 1:30 p.m. The Public Defender Agency was appointed. Preliminary hearings are set for Oct. 26 and Nov. 5.
The police bulletin also records an assault incident at the 100 block of the Steese Highway at Third Street at about 6:58 a.m. the same morning, on the same case number. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Felony theft charge filed after Johansen Expressway arrest
body: Maya Denise Hernandez-Mullen, 28, was arrested at the 500 block of the Johansen Expressway in Fairbanks at 4:44 p.m. on Oct. 15, according to the Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin.

The court file, opened Oct. 16, records one count of theft in the second degree for a value between $750 and $24,999, a Class C felony, dated Oct. 15 at Fairbanks. The charging document is a city police complaint.
An arraignment was held on Oct. 16 and the Public Defender Agency was appointed. Preliminary hearings are set for Oct. 26 and Nov. 5. She is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Felony criminal mischief charge filed over North Pole property damage
body: A court file opened on Oct. 16 records one count of criminal mischief in the third degree, for damage of $750 or more, against Dominique Dashea Frey. The charge is a Class C felony, the offence location is North Pole and the date of offence is Oct. 14. The file flags the charge as domestic violence related.
The charging document is an Alaska State Troopers complaint. An arraignment was held on Oct. 16 and preliminary hearings are set for Oct. 26 and Nov. 5.
No item on the trooper daily dispatch for Oct. 14, Oct. 15 or Oct. 16 corresponds to the case. The dispatch is a press feed rather than a record of filings. The defendant is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Court orders warrants after three defendants miss competency hearings set for the same hour
body: Three competency hearings were set for 11 a.m. on Oct. 16 in the same Fairbanks courtroom. In all three the court record states that the defendant failed to appear and that a warrant was to issue. The cases are 4FA-26-01786CR, 4FA-26-01902CR and 4FA-26-02061CR.

In 4FA-26-01902CR the court also issued an updated order for an examination on competency to proceed, and vacated a pre-trial conference set for Nov. 12 and a trial week set for Nov. 23. In 4FA-26-02061CR a pre-trial conference set for Dec. 10 and a trial week set for Dec. 21 were vacated.
A fourth warrant was ordered the same morning on a separate calendar: in 4FA-26-02058CR the court records that the defendant failed to appear at an arraignment at 8:30 a.m.
The record states a failure to appear and an order that a warrant issue, and nothing about the reason. All four defendants are charged, not convicted.

entries.title: First-degree murder charge dismissed after finding that defendant is not competent to stand trial
body: The first-degree murder charge against Brian Jeffery Davenport, 29, of Fairbanks has been dismissed after a judge found him not competent to stand trial. The charge was one count of murder in the first degree with intent to cause death, dated Jan. 20, 2026.

The Alaska Court System's weekly dispositions report records the case as disposed on Oct. 8 with the disposition "Dismissed. Defendant Found Incompetent." The court's online docket records the dismissal and the closing of the case on Oct. 9. Both are court records and they state different dates for the same disposition.
The case concerned the death of an 87-year-old woman in January. The Alaska Department of Law has published nothing on the dismissal.

entries.title: Nenana case carries three felony assault counts over charges dated Oct. 9
body: A case filed at the Nenana courthouse on Oct. 10 against Gregory S Ashley carries six counts, all dated Oct. 9. Three are counts of assault in the third degree for a repeat threat of death or injury, each a Class C felony.

The remaining three counts are driving under the influence, assault in the fourth degree causing fear of injury, and driving with a licence cancelled, revoked or suspended for a criminal offence, each a Class A misdemeanour.

Every one of the six counts records an offence location of Fairbanks rather than Nenana. An arraignment was held on Oct. 10 and preliminary hearings are set for Oct. 20 and Oct. 29. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Case against Cody Steven Rudolph-Munro resolved by change of plea
body: The case against Cody Steven Rudolph-Munro was resolved at a change of plea hearing on Oct. 14, and the court entered a criminal judgment or disposition order the same day.
An omnibus hearing that had been set for Dec. 10 and a trial week that had been set for Jan. 4, 2027 were both vacated.
The court file records that a plea was entered and a judgment issued. It does not state the terms of either.

entries.title: Troopers forward domestic violence charges to prosecutors over assaults reported in early October
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch records that troopers responded to a report of domestic violence involving multiple assaults in Fairbanks between Oct. 7 and Oct. 10.

The dispatch states that the person who reported the assaults provided photographs and other evidence to investigators, and that charges have been forwarded to the District Attorney's Office for review.
No person is named in the dispatch entry and no court file has been identified for it. A referral to prosecutors is not a charge.

entries.title: Troopers investigating an assault reported inside the Fairbanks Correctional Center
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch records that on Oct. 15 troopers responded to a report of an assault that took place inside the Fairbanks Correctional Facility, and that the investigation is ongoing.
No person is named in the entry and no charge is stated in it.

entries.title: Two court files opened after trooper drink-driving arrests, with no charge yet recorded
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch records two arrests for driving under the influence on Oct. 15. Jeremy Strangfeld, 39, of Fairbanks was arrested and taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center. Susan Waite, 63, of Fairbanks was found impaired after a vehicle went into a ditch at Farmers Loop and Farmers Loop Extension at about 6:36 p.m.

Court files were opened on both on Oct. 16. Each records one count as "charging document pending or not filed" with no degree of offence stated, and an arraignment set for Oct. 23. The court file does not yet state a charge or a charge class in either case.
Both are arrested and not convicted.

sources.label: AST daily dispatch, Oct. 15 and Oct. 16

entries.title: Two further Fairbanks cases closed on Friday
body: The court recorded a dismissal in case 4FA-26-01985CR on Oct. 16.

In case 4FA-26-02053CR the court record shows the case was disposed of at an arraignment on the morning of Oct. 16, with a criminal judgment or disposition order entered the same day and two later hearings vacated.
Neither closure appears in the Alaska Court System's weekly dispositions report, whose window ends on Oct. 12.

entries.title: Theft arrest recorded at the courthouse block on an older case number
body: Ruby Lou Sullivan, 40, was arrested on a charge recorded by police as theft in the fourth degree, under $250, a misdemeanour, at the 100 block of Lacey Street in Fairbanks at noon on Oct. 16.

The arrest is recorded on a case number opened earlier in the year. Six other arrest rows added to the same feed for Oct. 13 and Oct. 14 carry the same block and the same timestamp, each on a case number opened weeks or months earlier. The 100 block of Lacey Street is the block of the Fairbanks Courthouse.
She is arrested and not convicted.
